correctness.rationale: At the balanced state the exact real co-rotating Jacobian is the quadratic form \(c\|Tv\|^2-2\kappa\|Uv\|^2\). Its positive and negative indices are bounded by the ranks \(\operatorname{rank}T=2\) and \(\operatorname{rank}U=M\). If the polygon is noncollinear, \(T|_{\ker U}\) is surjective, producing a two-dimensional positive space, and radial prescriptions corrected by tangential vectors produce an \(M\)-dimensional negative subspace within \(\ker T\). The zero dimension is exactly \(M-2\), equal to the tangent of the regular polygon closure manifold by the submersion theorem. For collinear polygons, an orthogonal rotation separates \(c\boldsymbol1\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}\) and \(-2\operatorname{diag}(a_j)+c\boldsymbol1\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}\). Sylvester congruence yields eigen-sign pattern \(-2\) of multiplicity \(M-1\) plus \(2(\tau-1)\). All strict cases and equality follow without numerical extrapolation. The supplied standalone exact-rational verifier passed 3,504 assertions on finite examples; it is supplementary.

originality.rationale: The all-active balanced polygon family and real-coupling gradient structure are established in Zhao–Uchida (2026), but their analysis uses sampled Jacobians in a generally complex-coupling regime and does not give a universal signature or collinear threshold. Earlier mean-field Stuart–Landau studies give exact homogeneous splay/cluster stability boundaries or incoherent-state dynamics, not the present arbitrary-heterogeneity all-size signature trichotomy. The new claim is an exact complete index theorem for the particular polygonal manifold, not the invention of that manifold or the gradient system. Equivalent unindexed prior work remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent all-polygon Hessian/index theorem might exist in unindexed or specialized synchronization literature.
The current result does not extend to reactive coupling, inactive oscillators or Kerr terms; source numerics include those other parameter regimes.

value.rationale: The recently introduced balanced polygonal family is a natural candidate for stable or unstable coherent states. Exact inertia distinguishes two independent expanding transverse modes from an \((M-2)\)-dimensional neutral geometric manifold for every noncollinear configuration and arbitrarily heterogeneous positive radii. At collinearity it gives the sharp structural transition \(\tau=1\) in unstable dimension and nullity, e.g. \(c=\beta/6\) for the four-identical-oscillator opposite-pair state. This is a meaningful complete local classification across all sizes and parameters, not just a routine sign test, a finite census, or a generic gradient-flow corollary. It motivates interpretation of the special dissipative boundary of polygonal stability diagrams; it does not assert nonlinear bifurcation type or global attraction.
